25.00000,45.90000.desc: A decision on a living modified organism, filed by the country itself to the Biosafety Clearing-House. Article 20 of the Cartagena Protocol requires every party to file its release and market decisions there within fifteen days, and 173 parties are bound by it. The United States is not among them. Nowhere else holds national release decisions from this many countries in one place. A country with no records here has not necessarily approved nothing — it may not have filed, and from the outside those two look the same.

-96.95550,32.90980.name: IVFMD-Irving
-96.95550,32.90980.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Sy Q. Le, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

77.58414,12.93400.name: Cloud Nine, Jayanagar
77.58414,12.93400.desc: A clinic mapped in OpenStreetMap as offering fertility treatment. OpenStreetMap holds what somebody chose to map, so a country with few points here may be thinly mapped rather than thinly served. That is the reverse of the national registers alongside it, which are close to complete for one country and silent everywhere else. This layer is a cross-check and a source of leads, not a count.

-83.14465,42.48948.name: William Beaumont University Hospital
-83.14465,42.48948.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Part of Corewell Health. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-69.89184,18.47139.name: PROFERT Programa de ReproducciÃ³n Asistida y Medicina Perinatal
-69.89184,18.47139.desc: A centre accredited by REDLARA, the Latin American Network of Assisted Reproduction. Website: www.profert.health. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. REDLARA accreditation is voluntary and its members report to a shared registry, which is why Latin America can be read at all — most countries in the region have no national register of clinics. What it is not is a complete list: a clinic outside REDLARA appears nowhere. No street address resolved, so this point is the city or the country rather than the centre.

-96.80000,32.78700.name: Colossal Biosciences
-96.80000,32.78700.desc: The best-funded de-extinction company, valued in the billions, promising mammoths, thylacines and dodos. Read its own technology pages and the business is clearer than the publicity: the money is in the platform and the spin-outs — editing tools, computational methods, plastic-degrading enzymes — and the animal is the reason anyone funds them. Its conservation claims are contested by conservation biologists, largely on the grounds that the money would save more species spent otherwise. The April 2025 dire wolf claim was, by the company's own account, editing grey wolf cells already about 99.5% identical, cloning into domestic dog eggs and transferring dozens of embryos into surrogate dogs for three animals. The preprint appeared days after the media coverage.

-96.80000,32.78700.name: Colossal Biosciences — founders and scientific advisers
-96.80000,32.78700.desc: The named founders and advisory board of the de-extinction company, including George Church. The advisers matter because de-extinction has almost no regulatory surface — no product to approve, no release yet proposed — so the credibility of the people involved is doing the work that a regulator's assessment would do in any other part of this field.

-73.92000,41.31600.name: Regeneron Genetics Center
-73.92000,41.31600.state: Tarrytown, New York — 777 Old Saw Mill River Rd
-73.92000,41.31600.desc: Sequences the genomes of hundreds of thousands of volunteers linked to health records, in partnership with health systems including a large US one and the UK Biobank. Private companies now hold population-scale genomic datasets assembled with public and patient cooperation.

-92.30000,34.70000.name: LLRICE 601 — unapproved rice in the US commercial supply
-92.30000,34.70000.state: Arkansas and the US rice belt
-92.30000,34.70000.size: US rice exports; EU and Japan import suspensions
-92.30000,34.70000.desc: An experimental rice line never approved for sale was found throughout the US commercial supply, having spread from research plots years earlier. Exports were rejected, prices collapsed, and farmers who had never planted it carried the loss.

8.42600,49.50300.name: BASF — functional crop care and inoculants
8.42600,49.50300.desc: Sells microbial inoculants and seed treatments alongside its chemical and seed businesses. Live organisms applied to seed are a release in every practical sense and are regulated as a crop input, which is a lighter route than the one an engineered plant takes.

-0.17700,51.49800.name: Global Biofoundry Alliance
-0.17700,51.49800.desc: Links around thirty public biofoundries across four continents, most of them state-funded, sharing protocols and capacity. Public foundries put organism engineering inside universities and national laboratories rather than inside companies, which changes who is accountable for what comes out.

16.24500,48.21600.name: Romer Labs — AgraStrip GMO tests
16.24500,48.21600.desc: Strip tests and the extraction kits that go with them — tubes, buffer and a grinder, so a sample is prepared the same way every time. Sold internationally, which matters because the trait to test for differs by region: what is planted in Brazil is not what is planted in Spain. Same limit as any strip: it reads a protein, in fresh tissue or whole seed only.
